questions.q: In this lab's FAIR entry for risk R-014, what are Loss Event Frequency and Probable Loss Magnitude expressed as?
options: Single point estimates agreed on by consensus in a workshop
Colors on a 5x5 heat map
A pass/fail compliance score
Ranges, which get multiplied together to produce a range for Annualized Loss Expectancy
questions.explain: FAIR deliberately models loss as a range rather than a single number, and that range carries through into the ALE calculation instead of collapsing into one misleadingly precise figure.

questions.q: Why does the lab present Meridian's board with an ALE range of $18,000 to $840,000 instead of one number?
options: Because a single number would be easier for a CFO to use
Because ISO 27001 requires risk figures to be expressed as ranges
Because a point estimate would overstate precision that the underlying LEF and PLM inputs don't actually have
Because SOC 2 auditors reject single-number risk figures
questions.explain: A range stays honest about how uncertain the LEF and PLM inputs really are, while still giving a financial stakeholder something concrete to compare a control's cost against.

questions.q: What does mapping hardware-key MFA on privileged CDE access to SOC 2 CC6.1, ISO 27001 A.8.5, and PCI DSS Requirement 8.4 actually accomplish?
options: It satisfies three separate framework requirements from one control and one evidence package
It eliminates the need to ever test the control again
It only counts toward PCI DSS, since the other two frameworks don't recognize MFA
It replaces the need for a risk register entry for this risk
questions.explain: One control's evidence -- MFA enrollment and enforcement logs -- can be reused across all three audit engagements instead of being collected three separate times under three different labels.

questions.q: Why does the register entry for R-014 explicitly note a residual risk around the help-desk reset process, rather than marking the risk as fully resolved?
options: Because residual risk is irrelevant once a control like MFA is in place
Because MFA alone does not eliminate social-engineering risk against account recovery, and the register should state that honestly
Because PCI DSS requires every entry to list a residual risk regardless of accuracy
Because the help desk is out of scope for any compliance framework
questions.explain: An honest residual-risk note is what keeps a risk register trustworthy -- it records what a control actually does and does not cover, instead of implying the risk is fully eliminated.

questions.q: What is the actual deliverable of a mature GRC program, according to this lab's closing step?
options: A single risk scored with Likelihood times Impact
One perfectly worded policy document
A repeatable structure applied across a dozen or more register rows -- FAIR estimate, treatment, control, residual risk, and framework mapping -- not any single row
A list of every product the security team has purchased
questions.explain: The lab's point is that the repeatable method, applied consistently across the whole register, is the real deliverable -- not any one row built as a one-off example.
